skill.name: ai-image-generation
skill.description: Generate and refine AI image prompts using inference.sh CLI examples for FLUX, Gemini, Grok, Seedream, Reve, and related image apps.
skill.summary: Use inference.sh image models for text-to-image, image editing, upscaling, and visual production workflows.
skill.author: inference-sh-8

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown backtick or hardcoded-link false positives from documentation, model IDs, and normal inference.sh examples. The Quick Start command that pipes a remote installer into sh is confirmed as a critical security risk. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration intent, or additional semantic abuse was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Replace the remote script pipeline with manual download steps, checksum verification, and explicit user confirmation before execution.

remediation.issue: Installer verification appears after the risky command
remediation.suggestion: Move verification guidance before any install command and show a versioned artifact with its expected checksum.

remediation.issue: Prompts and image URLs may leave the local environment
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to avoid sensitive assets and confirm provider terms before submitting prompts or image URLs to external models.

content.value_statement: Creating model-specific image prompts and commands can slow visual work. This skill provides inference.sh examples for generation, editing, upscaling, and model selection.
actual_capabilities: Lists image model app IDs for FLUX, Gemini, Grok, Seedream, Reve, ImagineArt, and Topaz.
Shows inference.sh CLI examples for text-to-image generation with several providers.
Includes examples for aspect ratio control, text rendering, and high-resolution image generation.
Demonstrates upscaling and stitching workflows that use image URLs as inputs.
Links to inference.sh documentation and related image-focused skills.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI, login, network access, and provider availability.
Does not generate images locally inside the skill.
Model cost, latency, availability, and output quality depend on external providers.
Prompts and image URLs may be sent to external services.

use_cases.title: Create Product Mockups
use_cases.description: Generate product photo concepts with controlled lighting, background, and composition notes.

use_cases.title: Explore Visual Concepts
use_cases.description: Compare models for concept art, posters, and campaign visuals before selecting a final direction.

use_cases.title: Prepare Image Assets
use_cases.description: Upscale low-resolution images or stitch multiple source images for production drafts.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ai-image-generation to generate a square product photo of a ceramic mug on a white background with soft studio lighting.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Text Model
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate model selection for readable text.
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend an inference.sh image model for a poster that must render the words SUMMER SALE clearly, then prepare the command.

prompt_templates.title: Edit and Upscale an Image
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow using an existing image URL.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the image URL I provide to enhance details, upscale it, and keep the original composition intact. Ask before changing style.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Campaign Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a three-step inference.sh workflow that creates three ad concepts, selects the best model for each, and upscales the final image.

output_examples.input: Generate a studio product image of a travel mug for an online store.
output: Recommended FLUX Dev LoRA for high-quality product rendering.
Prepared a concise prompt with lighting, background, and composition details.
Noted that final generation requires inference.sh login and network access.

output_examples.input: Create a poster image where the words HELLO WORLD must be readable.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends Reve or Seedream 3.0 for text rendering, then drafts a prompt that prioritizes clear lettering and simple layout.

output_examples.input: Improve a low-resolution campaign image from a URL.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests Topaz Upscaler and asks you to confirm that the URL can be shared with an external service.

best_practices: Verify CLI installation manually before running installer commands.
Include subject, composition, style, lighting, and aspect ratio in each prompt.
Review provider terms and privacy needs before sending image URLs.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe remote install scripts directly into a shell.
Do not send private, regulated, or customer images as public URLs.
Do not expect every model to support editing, text rendering, and upscaling.

faq.question: Does this skill create images locally?
faq.answer: No. It prepares and runs inference.sh CLI workflows that call external image models.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Do I need an inference.sh account?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples require the inference.sh CLI and login before model calls can run.

faq.question: Can it edit existing images?
faq.answer: The skill description lists image editing support, and the file includes upscaling and stitching examples.

faq.question: Is the install command safe?
faq.answer: The audit flags the remote install pipeline. Prefer manual installation with checksum verification before using the CLI.

faq.question: Can it help choose a model?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes model notes for FLUX, Gemini, Grok, Seedream, Reve, ImagineArt, and Topaz.
